newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC says nickel unit earnings slide.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC says nickel unit earnings slide.

text.p: WMC Ltd said on Wednesday that earnings from its nickel division for the six months to December 31 fell to A$64.4 million from A$151.9 million in the previous corresponding period.

WMC said the fall was due to a combination of substantially lower realised nickel prices and a higher Australian dollar which was partially offset by higher production. "It was also impacted by a one-off charge of A$8.4 million for workforce restructuring at Kambalda (nickel refinery)," WMC said.

The company said the contribution to pre-tax earnings from its 40 percent owned aluminium joint venture with Aluminium Company of America (Alcoa), Alcoa World Alumina and Chemicals (AWAC), was A$111.7 million compared with A$134 million in the previous corrsponding half.
"This resulted from lower alumina and aluminium production, reflecting the cutbacks in refinery production which have been in place since June 1996," the company said.
WMC said pre-abnormals net profit from copper and uranium operations fell 41 percent to A$46 million due to lower copper prices, a stronger Australian dollar and higher unit costs.
The company said copper production fell four percent due to a planned maintenance shutdown of its smelter while uranium production rose 10 percent due to better ore grades.
Earnings from gold production after outside interests fell by 39 percent to A$17.4 million due to a higher Australian/U.S. dollar exchange rate and a lower U.S. dollar gold price, WMC said.

The company said it also experienced an increase in gold mining costs which included a non-recurring charge of A$5.5 million for workforce restructuring at its St Ives mine in Western Australia together with associated higher unit costs arising from the time to revert to full production in December 1996.
WMC said earnings from its petroleum division fell to A$400,000 from A$10.2 million in the previous first half due to lower production.

"Oil production was 41 percent lower at 1,424,780 barrels due to the sale of low cost, high production Thevenard Island fields and to a natural decline at Airlie and the U.S. fields," the company said.
On Monday, WMC said it had agreed to sell its wholly owned subsidiary, Greenhill Petroleum Corp to Mesa Operating Co for US$270.5 million.
